full_page.content:
1935, September
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 6.
Page 42 Cont.
Sep. 21 Baby John Riddmann - 8 mo. - very strange threatening blood-tuomer, birth-mark Drs. fear to touch it. Father a convert goes to com- munion 4 or 5 times a yr. They promise more frequent ... Sept. 25 Thank God! Baby decidedly improved; nor at all so restless when mother asks if he sould be taken to Dr. again.
Tillie Monske - 30 - Lutheran - fearfuly curved spine - Extremely nerveous - 2 operations in Ann Arbor.
Myrtle Huyler Butler - 43 -convert from Methodist ... asks prayers for oldest daughter 18, keeping company with undesirable non C. (lutheran)
Clara Myers - 38 - Unity ... Things brighter, pain in side, hard of hear- ing, hearing decidedly better.
Jewish lady in Eloise - palsey 8 yrs. - has 2 little children - since invalid husband cares nothing for her.
Page 43 Sep. 21 Rev. Francis Lynch - 28 - Heart trouble
Thanksgiving. . . Anthony F. Sales
Miss Louise Schoen - 70 - Enemic but well preserved - has been a real mother to, not only her brothers & sisters but as much as possible to her invalid mother now gone 15 yrs .... Drs. hopeless
Flora Cuseomano - 36 - very sick - stomach - although Drs. find nothing.
Mrs. May T. Strenger - 64 - in one Ford's Hosp. 4 mo., doctoring 18 mos. - some thought in cancer, now said to be tuburcular bone-spine, given up last Jan. Ist when enrolled in Ser. Mass Ass'n. Here To-day but very poorly.
Mrs. Mary Stege - 73 - of Bushtel, 0. - Jandis - - quite invalid since last October. Had 3 - 4 sons & nurse in World War. All came home together ... a shock of joy - Husband died in 1922.
Page 44 Sep. 21 Eulalia Hammer - 48 - was blind, August 21st inscribed in Ser. Mass As'n now almost O.K. Deo Gr.
